title: Fantasy-Relevant News Segment
description: Preserves the event, the source's interpretation, affected entities, uncertainty and short- versus long-term implications.
principles: Separate the reported event from the hosts' fantasy interpretation.
A short news item may remain short; a long debate must retain its reasoning.
Keep all substantive news segments, even when they are outside the headline topic.

dimensions.description: The news event or reported change.
dimensions.preservation_expectation: State what happened in source-supported terms.
detection_questions: Is it confirmed, reported or speculative?

dimensions.description: How the hosts interpret the event.
dimensions.preservation_expectation: Preserve the source's conclusion and reasoning separately from the event.
detection_questions: Why do the hosts think it matters or not?

dimensions.description: Near-term role, availability or market impact.

dimensions.preservation_expectation: Separate long-term view from immediate reaction.

dimensions.description: Players, teams, units, coaches or markets affected.
dimensions.preservation_expectation: Link direct and indirect subjects with relation context.

dimensions.description: Confidence, coach talk, reporting quality and unresolved details.
detection_questions: How reliable is the event or interpretation?

dimensions.description: ADP, trade value or sentiment response.
dimensions.preservation_expectation: Keep source price response distinct from player quality.
detection_questions: Does the source expect overreaction or underreaction?

dimensions.preservation_expectation: Preserve where the news matters differently by format or horizon.
detection_questions: Is this only Redraft, Dynasty or short-term relevant?

passing: Preserve the reference only where it is needed to understand another argument.
Do not create an artificial standalone evaluation.
brief: Preserve the conclusion and its immediate qualifier or condition.
Do not expand beyond what the source supports.
substantive: Preserve the conclusion plus the meaningful reason, condition, risk or uncertainty supplied by the source.
Keep format, price or time-horizon distinctions when they materially change the view.
deep: Preserve the complete major reasoning chain rather than only the final verdict.
Represent every materially discussed dimension, including competing positive and negative cases.
Keep disagreements, uncertainty, conditions and failure paths.
structural: Preserve the broad thesis, its mechanism, its scope and the subjects it affects.
Create independently reusable context takes rather than burying the thesis inside one player.

review_questions: Is the event clearly separated from the podcast's interpretation?
Are immediate and long-term effects distinguished?
Are all directly and indirectly affected entities represented?
Is uncertainty or coach-talk skepticism retained?
forbidden_distortions: Do not present speculative coach talk as confirmed usage.
Do not replace the source event with current outside news unless explicitly verifying.
Do not over-expand a passing news mention.
Do not omit a deep news debate because it is outside the episode title.
extension_signals: A new news type repeatedly appears.
The source uses a new reliability or rumor framework.
A recurring event-to-market relation is missing.
A mixed-news episode would improve reference coverage.
